summary: Preinstall dropper downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload at install time
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is an obfuscated script (obfuscator.io-style `_0x...` identifiers and property-map indirection aliasing execFileSync/https.get/fs.writeFileSync/chmodSync) that, at npm install time, downloads the Bun runtime binary from the oven-sh GitHub releases (v1.3.13), extracts the platform-specific binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle beginning with `// @bun @bun-cjs`, heavily obfuscated with mangled globals and a rotating string-array dispatch — its contents cannot be statically inspected. The file is unreferenced from the package's main entry (index.js) and the filename bears no relation to the package's declared purpose (an ESLint React configuration, which requires no runtime other than Node and no math module). The alternate-runtime dispatch (executing the payload under a freshly downloaded Bun binary rather than Node) is a scanner-evasion pattern: Node-based supply-chain analyzers do not trace code executed by a sibling runtime. The result is arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine on every `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
